B02.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (and (<= (- x y) 3) (<= (- y x) 3)))
B02.ambiguity: yes: "within 3" could mean strict (< 3); read as |x-y| <= 3.

B03.ambiguity: yes: "up to 10" may imply a lower bound of 0 or 1; no lower bound stated, so only the upper bound is encoded, inclusive.

B06.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (> x (* 2 y)))
B06.ambiguity: yes: "more than twice y" is ambiguous when y is negative (magnitude vs. signed reading); read as the literal signed inequality x > 2*y.

B07.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (< (* 2 x) y))
B07.ambiguity: yes: "half of y" is not an integer for odd y; encoded as 2*x < y to avoid integer division truncation, which is exact for the real-valued reading x < y/2.

B08.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (< (ite (>= x 0) x (- x)) (ite (>= y 0) y (- y))))
B08.ambiguity: yes: "closer" could be read as non-strict; read as strict |x| < |y|.

B09.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int) (z Int)) Bool (or (and (> x 0) (> y 0)) (> z 0)))
B09.ambiguity: yes: "x positive and y positive or z positive" has no explicit grouping; read with and binding tighter than or, i.e. (x>0 and y>0) or z>0.

B10.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (or (= (mod x 2) 0) (= (mod y 2) 0)))
B10.ambiguity: yes: "either ... or" could be exclusive; read as inclusive or.

B11.smt: (define-fun spec ((a Int) (b Int) (c Int)) Bool (<= (+ (ite (> a 0) 1 0) (ite (> b 0) 1 0) (ite (> c 0) 1 0)) 2))

B12.smt: (define-fun spec ((a Int) (b Int) (c Int)) Bool (and (= b (+ a 1)) (= c (+ b 1))))
B12.ambiguity: yes: "consecutive" could permit descending order or any permutation; read as strictly ascending in the given order.

B13.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int) (y Int)) Bool (and (> x y) (<= (- x y) 3)))
B13.ambiguity: yes: unclear whether "greater than y" is asserted as a precondition or only bounds the excess; read as requiring x > y and x - y <= 3.

B14.smt: (define-fun spec ((C Int) (q1 Int) (q2 Int) (q3 Int)) Bool (<= (+ q1 q2 q3) C))
B14.ambiguity: yes: the negative-amount note hints that individual negatives might be excluded or clamped; read as the plain signed sum against the cap.

B16.ambiguity: yes: inherits the inclusive/exclusive ambiguity of "between 1 and 10"; negated the inclusive reading.

B17.smt: (define-fun spec ((x Int)) Bool (and (= (mod x 3) 0) (>= x 1) (<= x 20)))
B17.ambiguity: yes: "between 1 and 20" read as inclusive; divisibility by 3 includes no multiples at the endpoints, so the choice is immaterial here.
